glossary.def: A value that divides the logits before the softmax. Low values sharpen the distribution toward the top token, and high values flatten it.
Limits sampling to the k most probable tokens. Not in OpenAI Responses or Chat Completions, and deprecated on Anthropic Messages.
A Chat Completions parameter that asks for best-effort repeatable sampling. It is Beta and does not guarantee identical outputs.
A map from token id to a value between -100 and 100 added to that token's score. Ids are tokenizer specific.
A string that ends generation when the model emits it. OpenAI Chat accepts up to 4. Anthropic reports `stop_reason: stop_sequence`.
A setting (`strict: true`) that makes tool arguments or structured outputs follow your JSON schema exactly.
A model output that names a tool and its JSON arguments. Your application runs the tool and returns the result with the call id.
A control (`reasoning.effort`, `reasoning_effort`, `output_config.effort`) for how much hidden thinking a model does. Values depend on the model.
A field that identifies the backend configuration behind a Chat Completions response. A change can explain different outputs for the same seed.
A Responses parameter that chains a call to an earlier response. Earlier input tokens bill again and `instructions` are not carried over.
A durable conversation object for Responses, released 2025-08-20. It has no 30 day TTL and is not ZDR eligible.
Reasoning items returned with `encrypted_content` in stateless mode, which you replay so the model keeps its reasoning context.
Setting `background: true` so a long Responses call runs on the server while you poll its status.
Supervised fine-tuning on input and ideal-output examples. OpenAI needs at least 10 examples and often sees gains at 50 to 100.
Direct preference optimization: training on preferred and rejected pairs with a classification loss, with a `beta` from 0 to 2.
Reinforcement fine-tuning, where a grader you write scores outputs. OpenAI lists `o4-mini` only.
LoRA applied on a 4-bit quantized base model, which let a 65B model be fine-tuned on one 48GB GPU in the paper.

claims.text: Claude Opus 4.7 and later use a newer tokenizer that yields roughly 30% more tokens for the same text, and the rise depends on content.

OpenAI POST /v1/responses/input_tokens returns an exact input count; Anthropic POST /v1/messages/count_tokens returns an estimate and returns invalid_request_error for server tools and the MCP connector.
GPT-6 models list a 1,050,000 token context window, 922,000 max input tokens and 128,000 max output tokens.
On the GPT-6 pages, prompts over 272K input tokens cost 2x the input and cache rates and 1.5x the output rate for the whole request.
Azure gpt-4.1 standard deployments allow 300,000 tokens and provisioned or batch deployments 128,000, although the model supports 1,047,576; max output is 32,768.
Azure gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.2 and gpt-5 list a 400,000 token context window with 272,000 input and 128,000 output.
Responses truncation defaults to disabled, which fails with HTTP 400 on overflow; max_tokens in Anthropic Messages is required and includes thinking tokens.
The Azure OpenAI TPM check counts max_tokens in full, so a max_tokens of 4,000 uses 4,000 tokens of limit even for a 200 token answer.
Reasoning tokens bill as output, share the context window and are reported in output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens; OpenAI and Azure advise reserving at least 25,000 tokens at first.
GPT-6 Astra rejects reasoning.effort none with HTTP 400, GPT-6.1 Sol has no none or minimal, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna accept none to max with default medium.
Anthropic output_config.effort takes low, medium, high, xhigh and max and is GA; Opus 5.5 thinking cannot be disabled.

OpenAI says to remove temperature, top_p and top_logprobs when reasoning effort is not none, while the Azure reasoning page marks temperature, top_p and logprobs as supported on the four GPT-6 models.
Anthropic temperature ranges 0.0 to 1.0 with default 1.0, and models released after Opus 4.6 accept only temperature 1.0 and top_p of 0.99 or higher, otherwise returning 400.
seed exists only on Chat Completions, is marked Beta and is best effort; Responses and Anthropic Messages have no seed.
top_k is not in the OpenAI bodies, is deprecated on Anthropic Messages and rejected on models after Opus 4.6, and Gemini exposes topK in generationConfig.

Anthropic's OpenAI SDK compatibility layer silently ignores seed, logprobs, top_logprobs, penalties, logit_bias, response_format, reasoning_effort, store and strict, and is for testing, not production.
Chat Completions stop accepts up to 4 sequences and is not supported on o3 and o4-mini; penalties range -2.0 to 2.0 and logit_bias -100 to 100.
OpenAI structured outputs allow up to 5,000 object properties and 10 nesting levels, require all fields and additionalProperties false, while JSON mode guarantees valid JSON only.
Azure OpenAI structured outputs allow up to 100 object properties and 5 nesting levels, and do not support minLength, maxLength, pattern and format.
Anthropic structured outputs use output_config.format with json_schema and strict true on tools.
OpenAI function calling suggests fewer than 20 functions at the start of a turn and tool_search with defer_loading for large catalogs on gpt-5.4 and later.
From GPT-5.4, Chat Completions does not support tool calling with reasoning_effort other than none; GPT-6 Astra and 6.1 Sol need Responses for tools.
Anthropic tool_choice any and tool return 400 on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, and with manual extended thinking.
GPT-6 supports async tool calling with async true on a tool, and the result returns with the original call_id.
Responses are stored by default with 30 day retention, previous_response_id bills earlier input tokens again and does not carry over instructions.
The Conversations API was released on 2025-08-20, has no 30 day TTL and is not ZDR eligible.
In stateless mode reasoning items carry encrypted_content by default and every output item must be replayed.
OpenAI Assistants API deprecation was announced on 2025-08-26 and the API was sunset on 2026-08-26; reusable prompts shut down on 2026-11-30.
Azure OpenAI v1 API uses a base URL ending /openai/v1 and needs no api-version.
OpenAI Responses stream events include response.created, response.output_text.delta, response.output_text.done and response.completed.
Anthropic streaming sends message_start, content_block_delta with input_json_delta, message_delta and message_stop, and tool input arrives one complete key and value at a time.
Under ZDR, background responses run with store false and data sits on disk for roughly 10 minutes for polling.
OpenAI Batch gives a 50% discount, a 24 hour completion window, up to 50,000 requests and 200 MB per file.
OpenAI began winding down self-serve fine-tuning on 2026-05-07 and active customers can no longer create jobs after 2027-01-06.
OpenAI SFT needs at least 10 examples with gains often at 50 to 100, DPO beta ranges 0 to 2, and RFT lists o4-mini only.
Azure fine-tuning offers SFT, DPO and RFT; training on the gpt-4.1 family ends no earlier than 2027-04-14 for existing customers.
LoRA cut trainable parameters 10,000x and GPU memory 3x against full Adam fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B, and QLoRA fine-tunes a 65B model on one 48GB GPU.
GPT-6 Astra costs $10 input and $50 output per 1M tokens while GPT-6 Luna costs $0.10 and $0.50.
Azure model router supports only Global Standard and Data Zone Standard, its effective window is the smallest in the pool, and version 2025-11-18 is updated in place.
